prologue.narration: She was the best student in her class. Not just good. Different. Numbers made sense to her. Patterns felt natural. Her teacher once said, quietly, "You think faster than most people I've met." She kept a notebook hidden under her pillow. Equations. Ideas. Questions about the world. She wanted to become a scientist.

prologue_2.narration: Every morning, she walked to school before the sun fully rose. Every evening, she came back just before dark. That day felt normal. Until it didn't. Her mother didn't look at her when she entered.

announcement.narration: Her father spoke instead. "You're getting married." Silence. She thought it was a joke. Then she saw their faces.

announcement_2.narration: "He is a good man," her mother said softly. "He can provide." "He is older," her father added. "That is better." She asked how old.

announcement_3.narration: "Fifty." Something inside her went still. "I have school," she said. No one answered. "I have exams next month." Her mother finally looked at her. "You won't need them."

react_calm.narration: She steadied her voice. "Can we talk about this? I'm doing well in school. My teacher says I could go further." Her father looked at her the way you look at rain you've already decided to walk through. "This has been decided." Her mother's hands tightened around her teacup. No one moved. The conversation was over before it began.
react_calm.emotionalResponse: Composure doesn't matter when the answer was decided before the question.

react_refuse.narration: "No." The word came out sharp and clear. For a moment, the room tilted. Her father's expression didn't change. Her mother flinched. "This is not a question," her father said, his voice lower now. Not angry. Worse. Certain. The kind of certainty that has never once been wrong, because no one has ever been allowed to correct it.
react_refuse.emotionalResponse: Refusal requires power. She had none.

react_leave.narration: She stood up. Her legs felt like someone else's. She walked to her room and closed the door. Not loudly. Not softly. Just closed it. She sat on her bed and stared at the wall. Through the door, she heard her parents continue talking. Lower now. As if she had already left the house. As if she was already gone.
react_leave.emotionalResponse: Leaving a room doesn't stop what's happening inside it.

pressure.narration: Days pass. The house fills with people. Voices. Plans. Decisions. Not hers. She tries again. "I want to study." Her mother sighs. "You've studied enough." "I want to become something." "You will. A wife."

pressure_argue.narration: At first, they listen. Then they stop. Then they get angry. "This is not your decision." "This is how things are done." "Do not embarrass us." The notebook disappears. Her school bag is moved. Her name is no longer spoken the same way.
pressure_argue.emotionalResponse: Arguing requires someone willing to hear you. No one was.

pressure_quiet.narration: She stops talking. She eats when told. She sits where pointed. She watches them plan her life like furniture arrangement. The notebook disappears anyway. Her school bag is moved. Silence didn't protect her. It just made her easier to carry.
pressure_quiet.emotionalResponse: Silence is not safety. It is surrender made invisible.

pressure_mother.narration: She finds her mother alone in the kitchen. "Mama. Please. You know I'm good at school. You know this isn't right." Her mother is quiet for a long time. Then she holds her. Too tight. The way you hold something you've already decided to let go of. "I know," she whispers. "But I can't." The notebook disappears the next day. Her school bag is moved. Her mother does not look at her again.
pressure_mother.emotionalResponse: Love without power is just grief with a witness.

escape_night.narration: The wedding is in a few days. That night, she doesn't sleep. She lies still and listens to the house breathe. She thinks of one person. Her teacher. The one who said she was different. The one who told her she thought faster than most people. She leaves before sunrise. Runs the same road she walks every day. But faster. Different.

escape_back.narration: Halfway down the road, she stops. The darkness feels heavier than the house. She turns around. Walks back. Slower now. Sits on her bed. Waits. In the morning, her father tells her the guests are arriving early. She nods. She doesn't know what else to do. There was never anything else to do.
escape_back.emotionalResponse: Going back was not a choice. It was gravity.

escape_hide.narration: She finds a place behind the market stalls. Cold concrete. The smell of old vegetables. She sits with her knees against her chest and waits for something. She doesn't know what. Morning comes. Then voices. Her uncle finds her before noon. He doesn't hit her. He doesn't yell. He just says, "Come." And she does. Because where else is there?
escape_hide.emotionalResponse: You can only hide in a place where someone isn't already looking.

escape_teacher.narration: She reaches the school. Empty. Quiet. Her teacher is there. She tells her everything. Every word comes out at once. "I don't want this. I want to study. I want to stay here. Please help me."

betrayal.narration: For a moment, nothing. Then her teacher nods slowly. "You did the right thing coming here." Relief. For the first time in days.

betrayal_2.narration: The door opens. Footsteps. Her father. She turns. Confused. Her teacher doesn't look at her. "She's here," she says. Everything becomes quiet again. But this time, it feels final.
betrayal_2.emotionalResponse: Even the person who told you that you were special was part of the system that decided you weren't.

aftermath.narration: Days later, the house is full again. But she is not. Not really. Her notebook is gone. Her school is gone. Her future is smaller now. Somewhere, numbers still make sense. But no one is asking her to solve them.
